subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: When a signature-validated SMS callback exceeds OpenClaw’s dispatch quota, should OpenClaw reject it for Twilio fallback/retry handling, durably queue it before acknowledging, or intentionally acknowledge and discard it?
rationale: This is an externally visible delivery-admission contract: code review can identify the consequences, but cannot decide whether operators should receive truthful failure, durable buffering, or deliberate loss.

options.title: Queue then acknowledge
options.body: Durably accept the callback before HTTP 200, then drain it after capacity returns so successful acknowledgment means OpenClaw owns delivery.

options.title: Preserve rejection semantics
options.body: Keep HTTP 429 when the callback cannot be accepted, allowing configured Twilio fallback URLs or retry overrides to handle overload.

options.title: Approve acknowledged loss
options.body: Explicitly accept HTTP 200 plus discard as product policy, document fallback suppression, and require exact-head production proof and owner sign-off.

recommendation.title: Queue then acknowledge
recommendation.body: Durably accept the callback before HTTP 200, then drain it after capacity returns so successful acknowledgment means OpenClaw owns delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged quota restructuring currently defines the admission boundary this PR changes.
